mapPolicy.realPlaceDisclaimer: Golmohar Junction is fictional and is not the real Golmohar Railway Quarters in Howrah.

promptRules: reserve blank flat areas for deterministic signage
no generated letters, pseudo-script, logos, signatures or watermarks
preserve fixed entrances, windows, levels, landmarks and prop positions
religious, caste, party and regional symbols appear only when narratively required and human-reviewed
do not use poverty, dirt, disability, informal work or crowding as visual punchlines

locations.name: Junction Square
locations.narrativeFunction: Golmohar's public stage, where official announcements collide visibly with traffic, trade, weather and argument.
locations.mapStatus: Present on all maps but with different centre points and road priorities.
locations.neighbourhoodVisualIdentity: A broad irregular crossing formed where a bazaar lane, municipal avenue, station road and filled canal path meet without agreeing on right of way.
architecture: two- and three-storey lime-plaster shop houses with shaded verandas
post-Independence concrete shopfront additions
corrugated tea-stall roof
crooked freestanding municipal clock
sensor poles installed at mismatched heights
historicalLayers: old raised path beside a former canal edge
successive statue plinths and removable plaques
fixedFeatures: crooked municipal clock with three independently replaceable faces
tea stall on north-west corner
layered public noticeboard beside tea stall
bus stop with one straight and one repaired bench
statue plinth whose attached identity plaque changes
four-way intersection with no visually dominant road
three sensor poles at inconsistent heights
drain inlet partly hidden beneath the south curb
comicFunctions: official foreground claim contradicted by physical background
public meeting turns into several private grievances
repeated small obstruction escalates through several systems
animals interrupt optimization lines for consistent practical reasons

movement: queues curve around shade rather than painted lines

weatherStates.summer: Hard white glare, short dense shadows, cloth awnings pulled low.
weatherStates.monsoon: Reflective brown-grey water collects first at the south curb and reaches the statue plinth before the tea stall.
weatherStates.winter: Thin mist softens the station road; tea steam is visible.
weatherStates.powerCut: Shop battery lamps and the tea-stall hurricane lamp create unequal pools of light.

compositionRules: establishing views preserve the north-west tea stall and crooked clock relationship
the smart billboard leaves a clean rectangle for later lettering
important dialogue receives quieter wall or sky space
crowd density changes by time but never obscures the physical contradiction driving a scene
never: every eastern Indian signifier crowded into one frame

locations.name: Golmohar Municipal Hall
locations.narrativeFunction: The layered physical body of local government and the main arena for records, grievances, ceremonies, power failure and negotiation.
locations.mapStatus: Tax, utility and property systems use three different parcel identities; one utility layer omits the building entirely.
locations.neighbourhoodVisualIdentity: An institution assembled from incompatible eras around a mature krishnachura tree, with level changes that require short ramps and improvised thresholds.
architecture: thick colonial-era brick foundation block with arched openings
1960s exposed-concrete wing with deep sunshades
late glass digital-service annex on steel supports
rooftop black water tank and patchwork aerials
generator shed built against an older boundary wall
historicalLayers: older council room and tree court
conference room refurbished for recurring schemes
digital annex connected through former archive cupboards
server closet inserted into records storage
fixedFeatures: krishnachura trunk enclosed by the inner courtyard
public grievance counter with metal grille and low writing shelf
archive room with high timber shelves and flood blocks
ceremonial conference room with off-level north wall
server closet inside a former records cupboard
generator shed with red manual changeover lever
roof tank visible from Junction Square
three floor levels joined by short ramps and two steps
comicFunctions: architecture reveals institutional history without exposition
new digital workflow physically depends on old cupboards and wiring
the same corridor hosts grievance, ceremony and emergency response
off-level wall provides the locked final visual joke

sound: server alarm muffled by wooden cupboard
movement: public queue switches shade as sun moves
staff use different stairs according to which wing has power

weatherStates.summer: Glass annex overheats while foundation rooms remain dim and cooler.
weatherStates.monsoon: Archive boxes rise on masonry blocks; water tracks down the join between concrete and glass.
weatherStates.winter: Low sun reaches the old council corridor and not the annex.
weatherStates.powerCut: Foundation wing retains daylight; server closet and annex require generator or manual procedures.

compositionRules: exterior views show at least two architectural eras
server-room scenes preserve cupboard doors, table fan, cable entry and changeover relationship
north conference wall is consistently 1.7 degrees off-level in the final sequence
sign plaques remain blank in generated art

locations.name: Rook Clinic
locations.narrativeFunction: Where administrative priorities meet bodily urgency and repaired technology demonstrates the difference between a workaround and neglect.
locations.mapStatus: Registered as a clinic, workshop and residential outbuilding in different systems.
locations.neighbourhoodVisualIdentity: A narrow ground-floor clinic in a shaded mixed-use lane, opening into a rear workshop court with a small solar array.
architecture: lime-washed front room behind folding metal grille
high grilled windows with green shutters
rear corrugated workshop canopy
small accessible threshold ramp repaired in two materials
solar battery shelf above flood line
historicalLayers: digital-result terminal added beside paper files
fixedFeatures: paper case-file wall behind reception desk
manual blood-pressure station
tap-sensitive analyser on reinforced side table
solar battery above marked monsoon height
rear repair bench with shadow board
waiting benches arranged around an unofficial social triage corner
water filter with handwritten maintenance card
comicFunctions: paper and digital queues visibly disagree
a sophisticated machine works only through specific maintained knowledge
clinical urgency defeats compliance ranking
repair competence is shown without romanticizing underfunding

sound: patients negotiating queue order in low voices
movement: Ananya crosses directly between patient and repair spaces
waiting order changes for visible urgency

weatherStates.summer: Green shutters half-close against glare; battery fan moves air across the analyser.
weatherStates.monsoon: Threshold ramp is wet; case files and battery remain above marked flood line.
weatherStates.winter: Front doors stay open and the rear court receives soft sun.
weatherStates.powerCut: Manual instruments and paper queue continue; solar battery supports only selected equipment.

compositionRules: keep medical dialogue backgrounds quiet and readable
show paper files and digital terminal in the same spatial relationship
do not crop Ananya's hands during examination or repair
sign fascia remains a blank painted band in generated art
never: dirt as shorthand for bad medicine
generated text on case files or signs

locations.name: The Twelve-Hand Market
locations.narrativeFunction: A dense economic system where price, freshness, weather, obligation, credit and bargaining resist one universal market value.
locations.mapStatus: No institution agrees on its official name, boundary or stall count.
locations.neighbourhoodVisualIdentity: A long bent market street opening into two covered courts, with trade grouped by material needs rather than neat administrative categories.
architecture: old brick godown walls reused as stall backs
timber and steel roof repairs from several decades
raised fish court with washable floor
open vegetable edge beneath tarpaulins
narrow service passages known only to traders and couriers
fixedFeatures: vegetable line at eastern entrance
raised fish court in south covered bay
hardware and mobile-repair row along old godown wall
medicine kiosk beside stationery stall
tea and sweet shops at central bend
improvised drainage channels marked by movable boards
three competing digital-payment placards at the same pillar
price chalkboards composed later as deterministic text
comicFunctions: multiple valid prices coexist visibly
prediction changes the behaviour it predicts
official stall sequence conflicts with practical trade adjacency
social credit helps vulnerable customers and excludes outsiders

sound: digital payment confirmation from several phones
movement: goods move crosswise while customers move lengthwise
walkways narrow and widen according to deliveries

weatherStates.summer: Striped tarpaulins cast strong colour blocks; fish court ice melts quickly into drains.
weatherStates.monsoon: Movable footboards bridge drains; service passages become important routes.
weatherStates.winter: Low-angle light reaches the vegetable edge and sweet-shop steam is visible.
weatherStates.powerCut: Cash, handwritten credit and battery lamps keep trade moving; digital placards remain visible but useless.

compositionRules: establishing shots show trade zones without presenting a generic crowd mass
each background merchant has a task rather than random gesturing
price and payment text stays blank in generated art
visual jokes do not depend on fish sellers, manual labour or bargaining being backward

locations.name: Golmohar Halt
locations.narrativeFunction: A place where official time, operational time, remembered time and anticipated time disagree in public.
locations.mapStatus: Officially upgraded to a junction; only one operational line passes through it.
locations.neighbourhoodVisualIdentity: A low suburban station stretched along one working platform, with an unfinished second platform and footbridge landing that leads to a locked gate.
architecture: railway-red brick station office
long corrugated platform roof
painted concrete benches
steel footbridge with mismatched repairs
unfinished platform edge reclaimed by grass
fixedFeatures: working platform on south side
unfinished second platform across one track
footbridge with locked north landing
stationmaster's office at east end
manual announcement microphone
digital signboard under centre roof
mechanical clock and digital clock showing different times
tea seller's stall near west stairs
comicFunctions: dog behaviour is a more reliable arrival cue than the digital board for observed reasons
junction status contradicts one operational line
manual announcement corrects digital certainty
passengers distinguish aspiration from prediction

movement: regular passengers position themselves from remembered carriage stops
dog moves to platform edge only after distant rail vibration

weatherStates.summer: Platform roof creates hard shade; rails shimmer.
weatherStates.monsoon: Wind drives rain under west roof; unfinished platform grows bright weeds.
weatherStates.winter: Mist hides track curve and makes sound precede sight.
weatherStates.powerCut: Mechanical clock and manual microphone remain; digital board goes black.

compositionRules: track direction remains east-west
station office stays at east end and tea stall at west stairs
Ghori's actions remain plausible canine responses to routine cues
all board and station lettering is added after art generation

locations.name: The New Development
locations.narrativeFunction: Prestige architecture that functions as a demonstration image while maintenance, drainage and occupancy remain unresolved.
locations.mapStatus: Fully rendered on investment maps, partially built on cadastral maps and absent from several service-delivery maps.
locations.neighbourhoodVisualIdentity: A geometric edge district of elegant gates, empty towers and office pods surrounded by invasive weeds, filled ponds and a road ending in mud.
architecture: tall pale concrete entrance frames
glass-and-metal model apartment pavilion
unfinished concrete residential towers
small sealed office pods
high surveillance masts
storm drains that terminate before the old canal
fixedFeatures: elegant double gate with no continuous boundary
model apartment beside security kiosk
two empty towers and one skeletal tower
functioning surveillance masts
nonfunctioning linear drains
perfect demonstration road ending at a mud embankment
office pods with active climate control and no tenants
invasive kans grass and vines
comicFunctions: camera works while drain does not
rendered future and physical present share one frame
optimized road terminates in unmodeled mud
empty infrastructure generates excellent performance data

movement: few people but many tracking cameras
delivery riders turn around where road ends

weatherStates.summer: Pale surfaces glare; empty pods remain mechanically cooled.
weatherStates.monsoon: Road stays smooth until its abrupt mud end; water bypasses linear drains.
weatherStates.winter: Kans grass catches low light and makes unfinished land look deceptively complete.
weatherStates.powerCut: Camera masts retain battery power longer than gate lighting or pumps.

compositionRules: clean geometry must be visibly embedded in unfinished land
avoid making emptiness look aspirational without physical contradiction
keep branded-looking surfaces blank and fictional
do not place real residents in humiliating contrast with model-flat imagery

locations.name: The Old Exchange
locations.narrativeFunction: Apparently obsolete infrastructure whose undocumented human maintenance supports modern communication and civic systems.
locations.mapStatus: Marked decommissioned on telecom records, active as a repair depot on municipal records and unnamed on public maps.
locations.neighbourhoodVisualIdentity: A shaded railway-era brick building behind repair shops, full of manual switchboards, relay racks and newer fibre equipment fed through old ducts.
architecture: thick red-brick walls
high arched windows with wire mesh
deep front veranda
cool switchboard hall
rear cable yard under corrugated canopy
historicalLayers: fibre interconnect hidden in old cable ducts
informal training space for excluded technicians
fixedFeatures: manual cord switchboard on west wall
relay racks down centre aisle
handwritten circuit books in glazed cabinet
modern fibre shelf mounted above obsolete label strip
battery bank in rear ventilated room
cable yard with numbered but text-free composition plates
repair bench beneath north window
comicFunctions: new service depends physically on equipment declared obsolete
diagram omits people who keep the circuit alive
manual patch solves a modern routing failure
safety criticism of old equipment is occasionally correct

movement: operators trace circuits by hand across racks
visitors slow down in narrow central aisle

weatherStates.summer: Thick walls remain cool; high windows vent equipment heat.
weatherStates.monsoon: Rear cable yard drips at marked points; sandbags protect battery-room threshold.
weatherStates.winter: Low sun reaches switchboard plugs and reveals dust.
weatherStates.powerCut: Battery bank keeps selected circuits alive; relay rhythm changes audibly.

compositionRules: preserve switchboard west wall, centre racks and north repair window
technical connections must be mechanically plausible
leave label strips blank for deterministic composition
show technicians as skilled workers, not relics
never: random cable tangles without circuit logic
all old equipment treated as safe

locations.name: Golmohar School No. 3
locations.narrativeFunction: A place where children, teachers, elections, flood displacement and predictive education collide with parallel records.
locations.mapStatus: Schools No. 1 and No. 2 cannot be reconciled across current records; No. 3 remains physically and socially active.
locations.neighbourhoodVisualIdentity: A U-shaped municipal school around a shaded courtyard, with old classrooms, a shared laboratory and later digital equipment installed against flood-marked walls.

high windows and ceiling fans
central courtyard with rain tree
small shared laboratory in converted storeroom

comicFunctions: scanner and paper register disagree in the same frame
